quiz.q: According to Atul Kohli, under which condition is the Indian state most willing to accommodate regional demands?
options: When movements express their grievances in linguistic terms rather than through religious demands.
When groups employ violent insurgent tactics to demonstrate substantial bargaining power against authorities.
When regional leaders demand sovereign independence outside the constitutional framework of the Union.
When organizations demand the complete abolition of asymmetrical federal mechanisms and local devolution.
quiz.why: Atul Kohli notes that the Indian state accommodates demands framed along linguistic lines, but firmly resists demands carrying religious overtones.

quiz.q: According to James Manor, why do strong ethnic identities in India rarely threaten national integrity?
options: Because the central government consistently suppresses all regional cultural expressions through coercive military force.
Because overlapping identities across caste, language, and religion prevent rigid, permanent social fault lines.
Because regional groups possess independent sovereign statehood under the provisions of the Sixth Schedule.
Because rapid economic modernization has completely eliminated traditional cultural attachments across all Indian states.
quiz.why: James Manor argues that overlapping and cross-cutting social identities prevent any single division from permanently polarizing society.

quiz.q: According to Paul Brass, what primarily motivated the centralizing features of India's constitutional federalism?
options: The boundless constitutional optimism embodied in Jawaharlal Nehru's famous 'Tryst with Destiny' address.
A conscious constitutional ambition to replicate the decentralized structures of traditional American federalism.
Pervasive anxieties and fear of separatism emerging directly from partition and communal violence.
A deliberate strategy to suppress regional political parties in favor of complete centralization.
quiz.why: Paul Brass contends that strong central emergency and financial powers reflected post-partition fears rather than pure constitutional optimism.

quiz.q: According to Rajni Kothari, what fundamentally drives ethnic upsurges and cultural assertions in India?
options: The competitive politics of state patronage driven primarily by electoral ethnic headcounts.
The culture of affluence generated by rapid agrarian modernization and economic prosperity.
The culture of scarcity emerging from severe economic deprivation in neglected regions.
A defensive reaction against the homogenizing project and excesses of modern statecraft.
quiz.why: Rajni Kothari views ethnic movements as a reaction against the modern state's drive toward cultural homogenization.
